# `Q-1-99` — Generic Validation Error

> A YAML validation error that does not fit any of the more
> specific Q-1-XX categories.

## What this means

Quarto's YAML validator has structured error variants for the
common failure modes — missing required property (`Q-1-10`), type
mismatch (`Q-1-11`), invalid enum value (`Q-1-12`), and so on.
This code is the fallback for validation errors that fall outside
those variants. The terminal message includes a free-text
description from the validator that explains the specific failure.

If you see this code, the validation system has a problem it could
not classify into one of the structured codes. The structured
codes are preferable because they enable better hints and tooling;
seeing `Q-1-99` in real configuration is a hint that a specific
code may need to be added.

## Why this happens

This code fires in two situations:

- **An edge case the validator did not anticipate.** Some
  combination of schema and input produced an error the validator
  could not assign to a known variant.
- **An infrastructural problem inside a schema** — for example a
  schema construct the validator has not yet implemented support
  for. Future Quarto releases will gradually narrow this code's
  use as such gaps are filled.

## How to fix

Read the free-text message in the error. It typically names the
specific problem with enough detail to identify what to change in
the YAML.

If the message does not point at a clear fix, treat the
`Q-1-99` appearance itself as a Quarto bug: the validator should
have produced one of the structured codes. Reporting the YAML
that triggered the error helps Quarto's maintainers add a
structured variant for the case.
